text:
Alex: heads up — noticed p99 jump on /generate in eu-west after yesterday's routing policy tweak. dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latency-eu-west :eyes:
Mira: saw it too. p50/p95 stable, p99 up ~120ms. quick glance at raw samples — counts look weird though
Priya: can you paste the routing change? my first guess is fallback weight increased and more traffic hit the quantized variant
Alex: change: eu-west primary weight 0.9 -> 0.6, fallback weight 0.1 -> 0.4 rolled at 02:30 UTC by the autoscaler policy tweak
Dan: that would explain more model-v2-quant traffic. quantized variant has acceptable median but heavier tail when KV cache misses
Mira: checked traces for p99 — ~75% include model-v2-quant, many show cold KV cache misses on first token batches
Alex: log snippet from router around 02:30 UTC:
```
[02:30:12] route_assign user=svc123 route=eu-west weight=0.6 fallback=0.4
[02:30:13] model_select request_id=abcd model=model-v2-quant
[02:30:14] kvcache_miss key=prefix_user_...
```
Priya: bench results earlier showed quantized variant p95 close to baseline, but p99 diverged for sequences >512 tokens. Wasn't expected to affect endpoint-level p99 so much
Dan: two amplifiers here: (1) higher fallback weight routing more long-seq requests to quantized model, (2) kvcache warmup pattern so early traffic sees full decode cost
Mira: also possible dashboard aggregation is amplifying the signal — our rollup merges tdigest snapshots that can be noisy when sample counts vary across shards
Alex: pulled raw sample counts for last hour: p99 calculation used ~180 samples, while p95 used ~12k. low sample count makes p99 very noisy
Priya: so both real shift (more quantized hits) and statistical noise (low p99 sample). we should treat p99 with provenance + sample counts visible
Dan: propose immediate mitigations:
- revert route weight to 0.9 (Alex)
- surface a sample-count badge on p99 in console (Mira)
- add per-model percentile split for endpoints so we can see model-level tails (Priya)
- run KV priming on canary to measure tail with warmed cache (Dan)
Alex: + action: annotate the dashboard with the routing policy change so future diffs show provenance
Mira: small UX ask: show a warning if p99 sample count < 500: yellow badge with tooltip "p99 may be unstable — low sample count"
Priya: agreed. also add a column on the route table for "fallback-hit-rate" so routing/quotas show immediate correlation to latency shifts
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Received request from Alex. Initiating rollback: route eu-west primary weight -> 0.9
Alex: thanks — i'll monitor. i'll also follow up with a short incident note in #incidents with the timeline
Priya: FYI for product — quota/backoff strategies that route to cheaper models can unintentionally increase endpoint tails. we should document tradeoffs for routing policy owners
Dan: long-term: console should expose per-model, per-variant percentiles and sample-provenance (route weight, quota fallbacks, kvcache-hit-rate) in the latency pane
Mira: agreed. I'll spin up a quick mock for the sample-badge and drop in the PR description
Alex: timeline: rolling rollback now, watch for p99 to drop in next 10m. if doesn't, we'll dig deeper
Priya: ACK
Dan: ACK :thumbsup:
Mira: moving to create dashboard annotation and a small UX PR after rollback validated
Alex: thanks everyone. follow-up thread with postmortem to include: routing policy change, sample counts, model-variant tails, console UX changes.
